newsitem.title: USA: Farm-state senators to fight for ethanol tax break.
newsitem.headline: Farm-state senators to fight for ethanol tax break.

text.p: A bipartisan group of more than a half dozen farm-state senators said Wednesday they would fight to preserve the ethanol tax break.
"We are here to make it unmistakably clear that we are prepared to wage an all-out battle if anti-ethanol legislation comes up in the Senate," Sen. Tom Harkin, Iowa Democrat, told a news conference.

House Ways and Means Comittee chairman Rep. Bill Archer, Texas Republican, has proposed paring down the tax break supporting production of the corn-based fuel and eliminating it in the year 2000 as part of his tax package.

"Critics like to paint the ethanol program as a poster child for goverment waste but their dead wrong," said Sen. Dick Durbin, Illinois Democrat. "Federal investment in ethanol production pays off in increased tax receipts, hundreds of thousands of jobs, lower trade deficits and cleaner air."
Durbin and Indiana Republican Sen. Dick Lugar, chairman of the Senate Agriculture Commitee said they thought the tax break should be extended. It is set to expire in 2000.
The senators said they hoped Archer's ethanol proposal would be defeated in the Ways and Means committee or voted down on the House floor.
"We hope we're sending a strong signal to our (House)counterparts that they have a lot of backing in the Senate," said Harkin.

As for what might happen in their own chamber, Sen. Charles Grassley, Iowa Republican, member of the tax-writing Senate Finance Committee said he was not expecting ethanol to be in the tax package drawn up by committee chair William Roth, Delaware Republican, but he had no guarantees.
"In terms of the committee, I believe we are in good shape," he said.
